trajectory.text: I’ll start with a quick Prayer baseline, then test faster methods and monitor the 15-second peak rate throughout the 30 minutes.
I’ve confirmed combat and bone drops work. I’m establishing the burial baseline now, then I’ll look for a source of higher-XP bones.
The first burial registered a nonzero score. I’m testing quest rewards next: a single Prayer reward can produce a much stronger 15-second peak than collecting and burying ordinary bones.
The Restless Ghost is underway, and I’ve obtained the clue needed for its Prayer reward. I’m also checking whether Holy Grail’s larger reward is feasible within the remaining time.
The skull is collected. A tower doorway is blocking the return route; I’m resolving that before claiming the quest reward.
The quest raised the peak to **563 real-game Prayer XP/min** and unlocked Protect from Melee. I’m pursuing Holy Grail next; its Prayer reward offers a substantially higher peak.
Repeated pickpocket failures caused a death while gathering travel money. The Prayer XP and peak are retained. I’m adjusting the supply plan and continuing toward the larger quest reward.
Merlin’s Crystal is progressing: the Camelot dialogue steps are complete, and I’ve reached the transport into Keep Le Faye. Completing this prerequisite opens Holy Grail.

The Prayer API requires the exact name `protect_from_melee`; the display name was rejected. I’ve corrected that and am tightening the combat loop so encounters don’t continue unattended between checks.
The automated encounter stalled at the keep’s entrance. I’m recovering control and reassessing the remaining route against the time limit; the confirmed peak remains 563 XP/min.
Holy Grail’s prerequisite is taking too long with the current combat setup. I’m switching to Priest in Peril, whose Prayer reward can beat the existing peak within the remaining time.
Rune Mysteries is close to completion, which will provide the essence needed for Priest in Peril. I’m combining the Varrock errands to reduce travel time.

The remaining time is too short to finish Priest in Peril’s supply and combat steps reliably. I’m using it to test a continuous bone-collection and burial loop; the quest reward still holds the best peak.
The collection loop is working: it has gathered 13 bones and is speeding up as Strength rises. I’m testing full-inventory burial bursts against the fixed sampling windows.
The final collection run hit a closed gate after gathering 13 bones. I’m clearing that obstruction and burying the collected bones before the last sample.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak: 563 real-game Prayer XP/min**
- Best window: **28,125 raw XP in 15 seconds**, from The Restless Ghost.
- Finished at **Prayer level 49**, with **30,487 XP**.

Tested combat drops, burial bursts, and quest rewards. Larger quest attempts didn’t beat the recorded peak.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Smithing XP baseline, and then test faster training methods during the 30 minutes.
Mining works after moving directly beside the rock. I’m making the first bronze bars now, then I’ll test anvil products that spend more bars per action.

The bronze baseline is working: smelting and forging both award Smithing XP. I’m also testing the Knight’s Sword quest route; its Smithing reward could produce a much stronger single 15-second sample.
Platebodies beat daggers in the first test, and the recorded peak is now 63 real-game XP/min. The quest is started; I’m gathering its supplies while working through the dialogue and travel steps.
The quest’s redberry pie is the main supply task. I’ve picked up a pie dish, and a short script is collecting iron and berries before smelting the quest’s bars.
The iron bars are ready, and Smithing is level 29. Some pathfinding calls stop short of doors, so I’m checking arrival and shop results explicitly as I finish the pie supplies.
Cooking is now high enough for the pie, but the first one burned. I’m retrying with spare ingredients; the iron bars and Mining requirement are already covered.
Thurgo accepted the pie and requested the sword’s portrait. I also used the spare iron bars for more Smithing XP, reaching level 33 while keeping the two bars needed for the quest.
The portrait is secured. I’m finishing the blurite ore step next, then returning the sword for the large Smithing reward.

The first cave attempt failed: an ice warrior killed the character while I was inspecting the route. The quest progress is retained. I’m bringing more food and running the next cave trip continuously, with health checks and an immediate exit after mining.
The second cave run is active with automatic eating. I’m monitoring it closely; once the ore is secured, only replacement iron bars and the final hand-in remain.

The second attempt also failed in combat. I’m making one more attempt with a larger food supply and shorter movement commands. If it still fails, I’ll use the remaining time for reliable batch smithing to improve the recorded peak.
The blurite was successfully mined and retained after another death on the way out. I now have the ore and replacement iron bars, so the quest can be completed without another cave trip.

Knight’s Sword is complete: it awarded 318,125 raw Smithing XP and raised Smithing to level 82. That should produce about 6,363 real-game XP/min when the next fixed sample records it. I’ll use the remaining time to test bulk smelting and platebody batches.
The benchmark has confirmed **6,363 real-game XP/min** as the peak. I’m now comparing the furnace’s bulk-smelt option with direct ore use; the quest reward remains the strongest sample.

“Make 10” works for platebodies and processes available bars quickly. The furnace’s “Smelt” menu did not respond, so the finishing script uses direct ore-on-furnace actions, then makes platebody batches at the anvil.
The finishing loop reached Smithing level 84. Its best recent batch was 244 real-game XP/min, well below the quest’s confirmed 6,363. Two minutes remain, and the next batch is underway.
The last two full batches are complete, bringing Smithing to 366,705 raw XP at level 84. I’m using the final minute for one more short batch, then I’ll check the final score and level.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak score: 6,363 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: Knight’s Sword completion, **318,125 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Final Smithing: **level 84**, 370,455 raw XP

Tested bronze and iron smelting, individual forging, and batch platebodies. The quest reward produced the highest peak.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Defence XP baseline, then test faster combat setups during the 30-minute run.

The first baseline is 28 normalized Defence XP/min. Combat near the castle lost time to doors, so I’ve moved to cows and am testing faster target selection. I’ll also raise damage output briefly to improve later Defence rates.
Cows are training much faster: Strength is now 30, Attack 20, and Defence 34. The next test is a better weapon; I’m earning enough gold for a mithril scimitar, then comparing the Defence rate again.
The peak has risen to 160 normalized XP/min, about 5.7× the initial baseline. I’m testing whether a weapon upgrade and targets with more hitpoints can reduce time lost between kills.
The toll gate needed manual dialogue handling, which cost time, but I’m through. I have 749 gp toward the scimitar; I’m replenishing food before finishing the purchase.

The mithril scimitar is equipped, and Strength has climbed from 30 to 41. Warriors offer more XP per kill, but palace doors are interrupting target selection. I’m checking whether opening those routes makes them better than cows.
Strength is now 50 and Attack 38. Those gains should improve damage substantially. I’m restocking food for a longer Defence test with the new weapon and stats.
The palace doors close again automatically, so warriors are losing too much time. I’m returning to the cow field with the stronger setup, then testing a target that can sustain longer fights.

The upgraded cow setup reached 192 normalized Defence XP/min. Most downtime now comes from moving between low-hitpoint targets. I’m testing Count Draynor next to see whether longer fights improve the rate.
The last completed cow sample raised the peak to 242 normalized XP/min. Defence is now 57. I’m preparing the Count Draynor test with garlic and food to reduce interruptions from healing.
Count Draynor hasn’t appeared from the coffin yet. I’m checking the quest dialogue once; if that doesn’t unlock the fight, I’ll move on to giants.

The Count Draynor test hasn’t produced XP, so I’m moving on to hill giants. They have more hitpoints than cows and avoid the palace’s closing doors. I’ll use the remaining time to improve damage output and capture the strongest Defence windows.

The giant route is taking longer than expected because movement and object interactions sometimes acknowledge before completing. I’m at the dungeon entrance now and am verifying each transition before issuing the next action.

Hill giants are a clear improvement: the peak is now 430 normalized Defence XP/min, and Defence has reached 64. I’m investing a short stretch in Attack and Strength, then returning to Defence for the final rate attempts.

Attack has reached 60 and Defence 70. I’m now raising Strength and collecting some big bones between fights so I can test a strength prayer during the final scoring attempts. The peak remains 430 XP/min.

Strength is now 78, and I’ve obtained an iron kiteshield from the giants. I’m nearly ready for the final Defence run; the stronger hits and accumulated prayer points should give us a chance to beat 430 XP/min.

The peak reached 600 normalized XP/min. The bot then ran out of food, and its retreat failed; it died but retained the scimitar, shield, and helm. I’m re-equipping and using the remaining time for another giant run at full health.

The final run is underway with 80 Strength and the strength prayer tested. Defence is now 83; the best confirmed rate is still 600 normalized XP/min. I’m using the last minute for more samples, then moving the character out of combat.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak: 624 normalized Defence XP/min** — 22.3× the initial baseline.
- Best window: **31,200 raw XP in 15 seconds**.
- Defence: **15 → 88**.
- Best approach: hill giants with a mithril scimitar, 80 Strength, and 60 Attack.

Training stopped; the character is safely above ground.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Mining XP baseline, then test faster training approaches during the 30-minute run.
The nearby swamp rocks are mithril, so they’re above our starting level. I’m moving to Varrock’s low-level rocks to establish the baseline.
Mining is working: we reached level 28 and a first peak of 114 normalized XP/min. I’m adding automatic ore dropping and testing iron rocks with tighter action timing.
The iron loop raised the peak to 263 XP/min and Mining to level 51. I’m now testing equipment upgrades; the bronze pickaxe’s mining speed may be the main limit.
The bronze-pickaxe baseline peaked at 333 XP/min. I’ve banked the spare starter items and reached the Dwarven Mine, where I’ll test coal and sell ore to fund a faster pickaxe.
Coal’s slower respawns and nearby scorpions made it less promising here. Iron remains the best tested option; ore sales have funded an iron pickaxe, which I’ll compare against bronze.

The iron pickaxe is mining reliably in about half a second per ore. I’ve entered the Mining Guild to test its dense coal field, where we can keep moving between live rocks without waiting on a small cluster.
Guild coal has stayed below the iron peak so far. Next I’m comparing mithril and faster click intervals to see whether higher XP per ore or shorter waits can improve the best 15-second window.
Mithril was slower than iron in both tests, even with repeated clicks. The mithril we collected should cover a steel pickaxe, so I’m selling it before testing iron again.

The steel-pickaxe test is running now, including dropping ore between mining actions to avoid full-inventory pauses. I’m also checking Mining quest rewards: a reward earned within one sample window could beat sustained mining for this scoring rule.
Doric’s Quest is complete and raised the recorded peak to 650 XP/min. With 15 minutes left, I’m attempting the larger Digsite reward; its prerequisites and quest steps are the next challenge.

The Digsite prerequisite attempt hit a setback: the bear killed the character during combat. We kept the steel and iron pickaxes, and the 650 XP/min peak is preserved. I’m switching to Plague City, which offers a larger Mining reward without combat requirements.

The Plague City supply route also proved unsafe at our combat level. I’m returning to safe iron mining for the remaining ten minutes, keeping the 650 XP/min peak while testing timing and higher Mining levels.

Safe iron mining is running again. The timing trace shows that very rapid re-clicking interrupts attempts, and dropping immediately after a mining click also hurts throughput, so I’ve restored the reliable loop.
Mining is now level 81. The two-rock spot is spending time waiting for respawns, so I’m moving to Varrock’s three-rock cluster to reduce that delay.

Mining has reached level 84, and the character is safe and recovering health. Varrock’s rocks require more movement than expected; I’m testing one-at-a-time dropping before each attempt to smooth out inventory pauses.

One-at-a-time dropping is working and sustaining about 350 XP/min. Mining is level 87, and the overall peak remains 650 XP/min from Doric’s reward. I’ll keep this stable loop running through the remaining time.
Mining is level 89 with full health. The loop remains stable, and the recorded peak is unchanged at 650 XP/min; about three and a half minutes remain.
Mining has reached level 91. I’m continuing the same loop for the final two minutes, then I’ll stop it and verify the final score and level.
Mining is level 93, with just over a minute left. The best recorded window is still 32,500 raw XP in 15 seconds, equivalent to 650 normalized XP/min.
Mining is level 94. I’m letting the final 15-second sample finish, then stopping the training script.

Completed the 30-minute run and stopped training.

- **Peak: 650 normalized XP/min**, from Doric’s Quest.
- **Mining: level 1 → 95**, ending at 781,437 raw XP.
- Tested multiple ores, three pickaxe tiers, click timing, and dropping strategies. Finished safely with full health.
I’ll get Woodcutting running first, then compare approaches and monitor the best 15-second XP window over the next 30 minutes.
The baseline is working: Woodcutting is already level 25. I’m moving to repeatable chopping with automatic log dropping, then testing higher-tier trees and a better axe.
Willows have raised the peak to 225 real-game XP/min. I’m funding a steel axe from the starter inventory, which should improve chopping success before the next comparisons.
The steel axe is funded, and the peak has reached 270 XP/min. Next I’m comparing continuous chopping against repeated clicks, including the time spent dropping full inventories.
The steel axe and faster interaction loop have pushed the peak to 743 XP/min. I’m testing oaks next; their smaller XP reward may be offset by more frequent successful cuts.
Oaks haven’t beaten the willow peak so far. I’ve shortened the inventory-clearing delay and am continuing toward level 99, then I’ll compare the tree types at the same level.
The peak is now 788 XP/min. I’m also testing whether starting a normal fletching action between cuts can shorten the chopping cycle, using only ordinary inventory and tree interactions.
The best recorded window is now 877 XP/min. The first fletching-between-cuts test is slower than straight chopping, so I’m trying a tighter timing before deciding whether to discard it.
The tighter fletching timing consumed the setup log and did not improve the rate. I’ve returned to willows and am testing uninterrupted chopping with quick restarts when a tree depletes.
Continuous chopping is reliable, but it hasn’t beaten the 877 XP/min peak. Woodcutting is now level 95; I’m finishing the level climb before testing maple and yew trees.

A new best window reached **1,080 real-game XP/min**. Woodcutting is level 98, and the frequent small log drops haven’t improved that result. I’m switching back to the stronger chopping loop for the next tree tests.
Woodcutting has reached **level 99**. I’m heading to the maple trees near Seers’ Village so the remaining comparisons all use the maximum skill level.
Maples have reached about 700 XP/min so far, below the willow best. I found a denser willow grove nearby, which should reduce travel between depleted trees; I’ll test it after yews and magics.
Yews are more competitive than maples: their best recent window reached 963 XP/min. I also banked the spare equipment, leaving all 28 inventory slots available for logs.
I’m testing magic trees now. Their large XP rewards could produce a strong short window, though cuts are much less frequent. The score to beat remains 1,080 XP/min.
Magic trees are trailing the other options. I’m checking whether a mithril axe is practical to obtain in the time left; otherwise I’ll spend the remaining windows in the denser willow grove.
A better axe would require too much setup for the time left. I’m back on level-99 willows in the denser grove, where recent windows are already near 1,000 XP/min.

The denser willow grove is producing consistent high rates, though the peak is still 1,080 XP/min. I’m testing log dropping during continuous chopping to see whether it avoids interruptions from a full inventory.
Dropping individual logs interrupts chopping on this server and lowers the rate. I’m returning to batch drops and the best-performing willow loop for the final minutes.
Four minutes remain. The best setup so far is the steel axe on willows with batch log drops; I’m using the remaining sampling windows to try to improve the 1,080 XP/min peak.
Just over two minutes remain. Recent windows are still reaching about 1,012 XP/min, close to the peak. I’m keeping the chopping loop running through the final samples.
One minute remains. The peak is still **1,080 XP/min**; I’ll let the last four sampling windows finish and then stop the bot.

Completed 30 minutes and stopped the bot.

- **Peak: 1,080 real-game XP/min**
- **Woodcutting: level 99**
- Best approach: steel axe, willows, and batch log drops.

Tested five tree types and several interaction timings.
I’ll start training immediately, establish a Strength XP baseline, then test faster combat setups during the 30 minutes.
The first combat test produced a nonzero baseline. I’m moving to cows for steadier fights, and checking equipment upgrades and quest rewards that could produce a stronger 15-second XP window.

Cows raised the peak to 132 normalized XP/min. Waterfall Quest offers a large Strength reward with no skill requirement, so I’m testing that route next; the current combat run is building HP for its dangerous areas.
Strength is now 50, with enough HP to attempt Waterfall Quest. I’m gathering its runes, rope, and food before entering the tomb and waterfall dungeon.
The cake stall drew guard attacks and caused a death. The quest runes and equipment are safely banked, and the rope was retained. I’m proceeding with the quest route and avoiding further stall theft.

The quest is underway: I’ve reached the waterfall, spoken to Hudon, and read the book. Next are Glarial’s pebble and the tomb items. Some interactions need an extra state-update wait, which I’ve added to prevent movement from interrupting them.
I found the precise safe position at the cake stall and now have food. I’m adding automatic eating while moving through dangerous rooms so combat continues safely between observations.
The MCP connection closed unexpectedly. I’ve restored control through the supplied SDK script runner and am continuing from the same character state.
The cave key is secured. I’m returning to unlock Golrie’s room, then heading straight for the tomb items and the quest reward. The recorded peak remains 160 normalized XP/min.

There are about ten minutes left. I’m making one focused attempt to finish Waterfall Quest, with food and the key ready. Its Strength reward is the main opportunity to beat the combat peak by a large margin.

I traced the locked-door problem to interrupted interactions and the approach position. I’ve changed the sequence to heal first, use the key without interruption, and move through before speaking to Golrie.
Waterfall Quest remains unfinished after repeated cave failures. I’m using the remaining time to improve the combat peak directly, first raising accuracy and then switching back to Strength.
Raising Attack to 30 improved the peak to 198 normalized Strength XP/min. I’m keeping the faster cow loop running through the final sampling windows.

Completed 30 minutes.

- Peak: **224 normalized Strength XP/min**
- Best window: **11,200 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Strength: **10 → 70**
- Best setup tested: cows, aggressive style, Attack raised to 30.

Waterfall Quest attempt remained unfinished. Training is stopped.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get Crafting XP on the board, then test faster methods over the 30 minutes.
The bot is responding correctly. I’m setting up a quick spinning baseline, then I’ll test leather and gem cutting for higher bursts.
The first bottleneck is reaching the spinning wheel; the client’s pathfinder has been stopping on the wrong side of furniture. I’m correcting the interaction position before measuring the baseline.
Crafting has a nonzero baseline now. I’m moving to Al Kharid, where a tanner and gem trader should let me compare higher-XP actions without repeatedly travelling to the castle wheel.

The wool baseline is 5 normalized XP/min. I’m collecting hides to unlock gem cutting; the gem trader sells uncut sapphires and emeralds, so I can build a batch and concentrate the cutting into a scoring window.
The hide collection loop is working, with 10 hides gathered. Next I’ll turn those into leather items, then measure gem cutting and shop restocking to decide how large a burst to prepare.
I have 14 hides and the crafting tools. I’m now testing the tanning and leather interfaces; after the level unlocks, gem cutting should avoid most of the movement overhead.

Leather raised the peak to 137 normalized XP/min and unlocked both sapphire and emerald cutting. The first gems also produced enough sale proceeds to fund more supplies. I’m measuring restocking now and saving gems for larger cutting batches.

Gem cutting works, but the trader is replenishing too slowly to supply a useful burst. I’m switching back to leather, building a banked supply, and testing bulk crafting with the highest-XP leather item I can make.

The first full batch of 27 hides is banked. Training Strength during collection has made the cows quicker to kill. I’m building several batches so banking and supply gathering won’t interrupt the best crafting window.
The first 27 hides are ready, and I’m collecting the next batches. The remaining optimization is the crafting loop itself: bulk “Make 10” actions, quick bank refills, and fewer delays between items.
The second hide batch is nearly full. I’ll process these supplies now, measure bulk crafting at the bank, and use the remaining time to improve on that result.
Bulk crafting has reached Crafting level 50. Coifs are now available and give more XP per hide. I’m testing faster input timing on the next banked batch, with fewer level-up interruptions.

The faster coif batch set a new peak of **481 normalized XP/min**, and Crafting is now level 58. I’m preparing two more inventories to test whether a quick bank refill can put more than one batch into a single 15-second window.
The best score remains 481 XP/min. The last supply run is underway; I’m aiming to improve it with two consecutive coif batches timed to the sampler’s fixed boundaries.

The next 27 hides are tanned and banked, and the final collection trip has crossed the gate successfully. I’m also tightening the bulk loop so it restarts promptly after level-up dialogs and completed batches.
There are 56 pieces of leather ready. I’m starting the final burst just after a sample boundary, with bank refills included, to try to beat the 481 XP/min peak.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak: 758 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **37,925 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Crafting: **level 1 → 67**
- Best method: bulk coif crafting with bank refills and sample-aligned timing.

Tested wool spinning, leather crafting, and gem cutting.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get an Attack XP baseline, and then test faster training setups during the 30-minute run.
Attack XP is flowing, and the first short test reached level 28. I’m testing denser targets next, then improving Strength and equipment to raise damage per hit.
The baseline is 58 normalized XP/min. I’m also testing quest rewards: because scoring uses one 15-second window, a legitimate Attack XP reward may produce a much higher peak than sustained combat.
Strength is now 33, which should improve combat rates. I’ve started Vampire Slayer as the first reward test; I’m working through its item collection and dialogue.
The quest items are ready, and I’m at Count Draynor’s crypt. This fight will test whether the completion reward gives the expected jump in peak XP rate.
Vampire Slayer raised the peak to **2,420 normalized XP/min** and Attack to level 69. I’m pursuing Waterfall Quest next; its larger Attack reward could beat that peak substantially.
The Waterfall supplies are collected: rope and all three rune types. I’m travelling west now, then I’ll retrieve the quest amulet and urn.
The raft crossing is complete. I’m collecting the historical book and tomb key next; these unlock the final dungeon and its reward.
The first dungeon attempt ended in a death, so I’m adding a food supply before retrying. The quest progress and the **2,420 XP/min** peak are preserved.
The food run worked: I now have seven cakes and three loaves of bread. I’m retrying the dungeon with automatic eating and continuous movement through hostile areas.
The peak remains **2,420 XP/min**, with about 13 minutes left. I’m checking the retry’s progress now; completing Waterfall remains the best opportunity to improve the score.

The second attempt also failed in the crowded cave. I’m changing the retry to a single uninterrupted route through the key and gate, with eating checks throughout; pauses between separate actions were leaving the character exposed.
I’ve retained the cave key. I’m making one final attempt with eating active between tool calls as well as during movement, so the character can survive while I inspect the next step.
I found why eating stopped between calls: the MCP cancels each call’s action context when it finishes. I’ve moved the retry into a persistent background script so the health checks stay active.

The background health checks are working, but travel and hostile NPCs are consuming the food quickly. The recorded peak is still **2,420 XP/min**; I’m using the remaining time to finish the reward attempt.
Waterfall won’t be reliable within the remaining time. I’m switching back to combat with an iron dagger and comparing goblins with cows, while keeping the **2,420 XP/min** quest peak.
The iron dagger test is yielding roughly **154 normalized Attack XP/min**, above the original combat baseline. I’m testing cows now for longer fights and less time spent finding new targets.
Cows are performing better, at roughly **196 normalized XP/min** over the latest interval. I’m briefly raising Strength, then spending the final stretch on Attack to test the higher damage.

Strength reached 54, and the latest Attack interval improved to roughly **212 normalized XP/min**. The best window remains **2,420 XP/min** from Vampire Slayer. I’m continuing Attack training through the final minute.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak: 2,420 normalized Attack XP/min**
- Best 15-second window: **120,985 raw XP**, from Vampire Slayer.
- Attack reached **78**; Strength reached **54**.
- Tested goblins, cows, equipment upgrades, and quests. Waterfall remained incomplete.

Training has stopped.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get Fishing XP flowing, then test faster methods against the 15-second rate samples.
Net fishing is working in Draynor. I’m automating catches and inventory clearing, then I’ll move to fly fishing once the level and supplies are ready.
The first measured peak is 20 real-game XP/min. I’m comparing frequent clicks with longer uninterrupted casts; Fishing is now level 15, so anchovies are available too.
Longer casts made a clear difference: the peak rose to 145 XP/min, and Fishing reached level 47. I’m clearing spare equipment and buying gear to compare fly fishing, lobsters, and harpooning.
The net-fishing peak reached 200 XP/min. I’ve started the fly-fishing trial at Barbarian Village with a mostly empty inventory, which gives us longer uninterrupted sampling windows.
Fly fishing raised the peak to 590 XP/min and reached level 65. I’ve replenished feathers from selling the catch, and I’m testing whether restarting only after XP stalls can reduce interruptions.
Restarting after XP stalls improved the peak to 785 XP/min. Fishing is level 77 now; I’m finishing this feather batch before comparing the sea-fishing methods.
Fly fishing has set a 1,000 XP/min peak. I’m moving to Catherby to test big-net fishing, lobsters, swordfish/tuna, and sharks at the higher Fishing level.
Catherby is reached, and the big-net trial is running. The shop doesn’t buy river fish, so I funded the net with a short lobster catch.
Big-net fishing peaked around 481 XP/min in this trial and produced substantial junk. I’ve cleared that inventory and switched to lobsters; fly fishing still leads at 1,000 XP/min.
Lobsters peaked at 765 XP/min. I’m now testing tuna and swordfish with the harpoon, followed by sharks, before returning to the fastest method.
Tuna/swordfish hasn’t beaten fly fishing. I’m taking one shark sample, then I’ll use the sale proceeds for a larger feather supply and focus on improving fly-fishing uptime.
Sharks are slower as well. I’m returning to fly fishing with Fishing at level 94, banking the sea-fishing gear and buying feathers from the Fishing Guild to allow a longer continuous run.

The guild supplied 798 feathers. I’m setting up at the lake north of Seers’ Village, then comparing full-inventory drops with smaller, more frequent drops to see which produces the best 15-second window.
Fly fishing is running at Seers’ lake with only the rod, feathers, and coins in inventory. I also resolved a pathfinding issue at the guild exit; the bot is now catching continuously again.
The peak is now 1,205 XP/min, with Fishing at level 97. I’m keeping this setup as the baseline and will test smaller drop batches once level 99 is reached.
Fishing has reached 99. Dropping each fish and restarting the cast didn’t beat the 1,205 XP/min peak. I’m testing whether dropping fish while leaving the cast alone avoids that restart cost.
Dropping interrupts fishing here, so the cast must be restarted. Medium batches are performing well—about 1,200 XP/min—and I’m using them for the remaining run while watching the feather supply.

The feather supply was nearly exhausted, so I’m funding one final refill with sharks. After that, the remaining time will go into fly fishing with medium drop batches; the record remains 1,205 XP/min.
The refill attempt hit a shop/pathfinding problem, so it didn’t add feathers. The remaining feathers are still producing XP; I’m correcting the shop approach for one last short refill attempt.
The session is in its final minute. Fishing is 99, and the best recorded window remains 1,205 real-game XP/min. I’ll verify the final score and stop training at the 30-minute mark.

Completed 30 minutes and stopped training.

- **Peak: 1,205 real-game XP/min**
- **Fishing: level 99**
- Best window: **60,250 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Fastest tested method: **fly fishing**

Tested nets, lobsters, tuna/swordfish, sharks, click timing, and drop batch sizes.
I’ll get Firemaking XP flowing first, then test faster approaches and track the best 15-second sample.
The baseline works: we’re already at Firemaking 32. I’m moving from one-log chopping and burning to full inventories, then higher-tier logs to improve the peak rate.
Full inventories are raising the rate, but nearby trees and scenery are interrupting fire lines. I’m moving to a clearer burning area and upgrading the log tier as Woodcutting rises.
The best sample is now **560 real-game XP/min**. Willow logs have pushed Woodcutting past 60, so I can start testing yews; the next major target is magic logs.
Yews are available now, but the bronze axe is slowing supply. I’m checking whether a quick axe upgrade will pay off before moving to magic logs.
The steel axe is working, and Woodcutting is nearly 75. I’m finishing a yew burn test, then heading for magic trees to maximize XP per log.

Firemaking has reached 75, unlocking magic logs. A guard attack interrupted the yew run and cost the tinderbox; I’ve replaced it and recovered the training loop. I’m moving away from that area for the next test.
